Subject: Dedicated capacity clarifications for Section C (RFP)

Hi Nikhil — thanks again for taking our RFP. A few items we need clarified before our procurement review next week: 

- Which GPU families do you recommend for a production fleet serving our mixed workload (short chat queries ~30 tokens, and generation jobs ~512 tokens)? We saw A100, H100 and L4 listed in your catalog; curious about latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- For capacity planning, how should we convert your reserved GPU commitments to expected QPS and token throughput? We need a band for sustained and burst (20% and 100% bursts).
- What is your suggested commitment phasing (3-6-12 months) for a first-year contract to balance cost vs. runway risk?
- Any constraints on burst (seconds of warmup, pre-warming GPU state, KV cache priming)?

Attached: EdgeGate_RFP_SectionC.pdf (we referenced the dedicated capacity section)

Appreciate a short writeup we can share with procurement.

Best,
Tom
Tom Li
Head of Platform — EdgeGate AI

- KV/prefix cache warmup expectations and recommended pre-warm steps for canary

Quick draft notes from my side (putting in plain language for procurement):

- GPU recommendations: H100 (best latency/throughput for 512-token gen), A100 (strong price-performance for steady-state medium workloads), L4 (cost-efficient for high-QPS short prompts and reranking).
- Conversion heuristics (per 1 GPU, causal 13B-ish model):
  * Short chat (<=64 tokens): ~350–450 qps (small batches, aggressive batching depends on latency SLO).
  * Medium gen (512 tokens): ~12–18 requests per minute (rpm) when aiming for 95th <150ms on H100; on A100 expect ~8–12 rpm for similar tail.
  * Tokens/sec approximation: H100 ~55k tokens/s sustained (steady generation pipelines with batching); A100 ~35k tokens/s. These are ballpark and depend on model and quantization.
- Burst guidance: short bursts (up to 20% above sustained) are handled by autoscaling + burst pool; large bursts (100%+ sustained) require warmup windows (30–90s depending on cache priming).

I'll turn this into a 1-page summary for Tom and attach the workbook. Dev, please confirm the token/sec numbers and any caveats for quantized models.

—Marissa

Tom / EdgeGate team — thanks for the clear list. Attached are: 1) redwood-edgegate-dedicated-capacity-response.xlsx (detailed conversion tables and throughput assumptions), and 2) commitment-phasing-outline.pdf (recommended three-phase commitment and operational notes). Summary below for procurement to copy into their packet: 

Executive summary (short):
- Recommended starting profile: mix of 24 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (cost-efficient steady-state) + a 12-GPU reserved H100 buffer for latency-sensitive generation. This mix covers a common hybrid workload: high-QPS short prompts + medium-length gen.
- Expected throughput (representative, per GPU, 13B-class causal model):
  * H100: ~12–18 gen requests/min for 512-token tasks (95th p95 <120ms typical with batching and KV cache warm), ~40k tokens/sec aggregate when batched.
  * A100: ~8–12 gen requests/min for 512-token tasks (p95 ~140–180ms depending on batch), ~28–36k tokens/sec.
  * L4: best used for short queries where per-request overhead dominates — up to ~400 qps per L4 on chat-size prompts when batching is enabled.
- Burst behavior and constraints:
  * Soft-burst (<=20% above reserved runrate): handled by autoscaling within reserved pool; no extra capacity commitment required.
  * Hard-burst (>=100%): supported via burst lanes (subject to availability) — we recommend reserving a modest burst buffer (10–15% of committed GPUs) for predictable peak events. Warmup: KV/prefix cache priming typically needs 30–90s depending on dataset locality; model weights are resident in GPU but KV caches require runtime population.
- Commitment phasing recommendation (balanced risk/cost):
  * Phase 1 (Months 0–3): Reserve 40% of target fleet (10 A100-eq + 4 H100-eq). Validate with canary workload and production traces.
  * Phase 2 (Months 4–9): Increase to 70% based on observed steady-state and tail metrics; enable quantized instances for non-critical inference to reduce cost.
  * Phase 3 (Months 10–12): Reach full committed capacity, add small reserved L4 pool for short-query offload where cost matters.
- Operational playbook highlights: canary rollouts (5–10% of traffic), telemetry hooks (token-level cost, KV hit rates), automatic fallback (A100->L4 for non-latency-critical paths), and negotiated SLAs for 95th/99th latency.
- Pricing and credits: attached workbook maps committed GPUs to blended effective unit price and shows savings at 12-month vs 3-month tenors.

Attachments: redwood-edgegate-dedicated-capacity-response.xlsx (conversion tables + scenarios), commitment-phasing-outline.pdf (one-page timeline and ops checklist).

If helpful, we can run a short 60-minute sizing workshop later this week to walk procurement and infra through the workbook. Proposed times attached as a Calendly link in the Drive doc.

Thanks — happy to iterate on phasing or swap more H100 for A100 depending on your cost targets.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
